betterquesting:10.desc:8:
In order to obtain more exotic particles than simple protons, neutrons, and electrons, you will need the Large Hadron Collider. You can use any charged particle as input, sourced from any other beam-like multiblock such as the Source Chamber.

The LHC's four modules can each produce a different set of particles. For a particle to become eligible for output, the §bCollision Energy§r must be at least the particle's §dRest Mass§r, shown on its tooltip in NEI. Particles with a §dRest Mass§r below 0.5 MeV still require at least 0.5 MeV of §bCollision Energy§r.

The LHC has two modes: §lAccelerator§r and §lCollider§r.

First, in §lAccelerator§r mode, it accelerates the input beam to a higher energy. It does this in 1-second cycles, with more energy added per cycle as the §9Number of Completed Cycles§r increases. The power draw increases quadratically as the §9Number of Completed Cycles§r increases, and linearly as the §cAmount§r increases.

You can set a target §6Beam Energy§r and a maximum §9Number of Cycles§r in the UI. The beam itself is capped at 1 TeV, so keep the target at or below 1 TeV. Setting a higher target prevents the §cAmount§r from growing. If your beam reaches the target §6Beam Energy§r before reaching the maximum cycle count, further completed cycles increase the beam's §cAmount§r instead, which also increases your power draw. Below 15,000, each of these cycles multiplies the §cAmount§r by 1.3, rounded up. At or above 15,000, each cycle instead adds (0.3 × current Amount)^0.5, rounded up. Once the maximum §9Number of Cycles§r is reached, the LHC automatically switches to §lCollider§r mode.

Later on, you can improve this scaling by supplying a Booster Fluid through an Input Hatch and selecting it under §lBeam Booster§r in the UI. Degenerate Quark-Gluon Plasma raises the exponent in the formula from 0.5 to 0.7, while Molten Magmatter raises it to 0.9. This lets you reach much higher §cAmounts§r with additional cycles.

Using either Booster Fluid immediately sets the §6Beam Energy§r to 1 TeV. As long as your target is at or below 1 TeV, the acceleration cycles can increase the §cAmount§r right from the start. The LHC consumes 1L of fluid per current §cAmount§r every second, in both §lAccelerator§r and §lCollider§r modes. For example, an §cAmount§r of 20,000 requires 20,000 L/s. As the §cAmount§r grows, so does the fluid consumption. If there is not enough fluid for the next cycle, the machine shuts down.

Changing the §lBeam Booster§r setting requires restarting the machine and accelerating a new beam from scratch. You can also select Booster Fluids in the built in calculator to see how they affect the final beam and power draw before committing to a run.


In §lCollider§r mode, the beam is collided with itself to generate all kinds of particles. Each LHC Module is able to detect and capture a certain subset of particles, depending on which Fundamental Force the particle can interact with. This also means some particles appear in multiple modules. You can blacklist particles from appearing by using the Filtered Beamline Output Hatch.

§l[note]§lThe §b§lCollision Energy§r §lis 2x the accelerated §6§lBeam Energy§r§l, up to a maximum of 2 TeV.§r[/note]
